decisions.question: What new React component is needed for the Search page master/detail layout?
decisions.answer: Create /home/anshulverma/workspace/workbench/ui/src/pages/Search.tsx with master/detail split: left panel (340px sticky) shows filtered results grid, right panel shows selected item detail with LLM summary, contextual payload, processing log, and actions. Pattern follows existing Triage.tsx layout but with kind filtering instead of priority/source filters.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype specifies this exact structure. Current codebase has no Search.tsx. The master/detail pattern is proven in Triage.tsx (filter rail + card feed + detail). All dependencies exist: router, hooks, primitives.

decisions.question: What new sub-components are needed for contextual payload rendering?
decisions.answer: Create four context renderer components inside Search.tsx: DiffContext (author/team/status/hunks using existing DiffHunks component), EmailContext (from/to/when/body in definition list), MeetingContext (when/where/attendees/agenda), ChatContext (channel + message list). Plus a dispatcher component ItemContext that switches on ctx.type. These render the source-type-specific payload from raw_data.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype shows all four renderers with exact structure. DiffHunks component already exists and can be reused. Pattern is straightforward conditional rendering based on item kind. Follows the established pattern from TriageDetail.tsx which already renders diff card_content.

decisions.question: What component renders the full item detail in the right panel?
decisions.answer: Create SearchItemDetail component with sections: (1) header with kind icon, ID, priority badge, state dot, source, timestamp, summary, tags; (2) actions bar with priority select, Mark done, Snooze 4h, Archive, Delete buttons; (3) LLM summary section ("Why this matters to you"); (4) contextual payload card using ItemContext dispatcher; (5) processing log card with funnel stages. Empty state when no item selected.
decisions.rationale: Design spec clearly defines this structure. All pieces exist: priority select from ActionItems.tsx, action buttons patterns from ActionItems.tsx and useItems hook, funnel stages will come from FunnelStage component (branch 3), LLM summary and tags are new fields but straightforward rendering.

decisions.question: What component renders individual search result rows?
decisions.answer: Create ResultRow component: clickable card with kind icon (lucide), item ID (mono), priority badge, state dot (triaged/pending_triage/action_item/dropped/archived with color coding), summary text, and footer with source + relative time + relevance score percentage. Active state via boolean prop for selection highlighting.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype defines exact structure. Pattern mirrors ActionRow from ActionItems.tsx and result rows from TriageDetail.tsx. All primitives exist (Badge, Mono, relativeTime utility, lucide icons). State dot is new but simple color-coded component.

decisions.question: Do we need a new StateDot component for item state visualization?
decisions.answer: Yes, create StateDot component in Search.tsx: small colored dot + label for item states (triaged=green, pending_triage=tertiary, action_item=primary, dropped=red, archived=muted). Similar to HealthBadge pattern but for ItemStatus enum values.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype shows state dots throughout search results and detail view. Current codebase has HealthBadge with similar pattern (colored indicator + label). ItemStatus enum already defined in domain/enums.py. Simple mapping from status to color/label.

decisions.question: What new API endpoint is needed for full-text search with rich item data?
decisions.answer: Extend existing GET /api/search to support a new mode: when a new query param full=true is passed, return full Item records with llm_summary, raw_data (context payload), processing_log (funnel stages), and verdict fields. Current endpoint returns minimal SearchHit records for command palette. Alternative: create GET /api/items/search with full records only.
decisions.rationale: Current /api/search exists but returns minimal SearchHit records (id, kind, label, sublabel, route) for command palette. Search page needs full Item records with contextual payload, LLM summary, funnel log, and verdict. Two options: (1) add full=true param to existing endpoint or (2) create new endpoint. Option 2 is cleaner separation but duplicates search logic. Design prototype shows searchItems[] with full records distinct from command palette SearchHits.

decisions.question: What new database fields are needed on items table for search page data?
decisions.answer: Add four JSONB columns to items table via Alembic migration: llm_summary TEXT (personalized summary), enriched_context JSONB (source-type-specific payload: diff hunks, email body, meeting agenda, chat messages), processing_log JSONB (array of funnel stage records), verdict JSONB (final decision with priority, confidence, rationale). Tags as TEXT[] array.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype shows searchItems with these exact fields. Current Item model has raw_data dict but design shows structured enriched_context separate from raw. Processing log and verdict are new concepts for provenance tracking. LLM summary is personalized explanation field. All are JSONB/TEXT suitable for PostgreSQL storage. Migration pattern established in codebase.

decisions.question: What new TypeScript types are needed for search page?
decisions.answer: Define in Search.tsx or new types file: SearchItem (extends Item with llm_summary, enriched_context, processing_log, verdict, tags), ItemContext union type (DiffContext | EmailContext | MeetingContext | ChatContext), ProcessingStage (filterId, outcome, confidence?, reason, context?, weak?), Verdict (decision, priority, confidence, rationale), ItemKind enum (diff, email, meeting, chat), ItemState enum (triaged, pending_triage, action_item, dropped, archived).
decisions.rationale: Design prototype defines all these shapes in searchItems[] and funnelItems[]. Current Item interface in useItems.ts is minimal. Need rich types for the extended search data. Context union follows established pattern from triage card_content. Processing log and verdict are new domain concepts. TypeScript enums for kind/state ensure type safety.

decisions.question: What new TanStack Query hooks are needed?
decisions.answer: Create in new useSearch.ts or extend existing: useSearchItems(q, kind) -> GET /api/items/search or /api/search?full=true (returns SearchItem[], 15s poll when query non-empty), useUpdateItem(id) -> PATCH /api/items/{id} (for priority/status/summary updates), useSnoozeItem(id) -> POST /api/items/{id}/snooze, useArchiveItem(id) -> DELETE /api/items/{id}. Some may already exist in useItems.ts and just need exposure.
decisions.rationale: Current useSearch hook exists but for command palette (SearchHit records). Need separate hook for full search items or extend with mode parameter. Update/snooze/archive actions shown in design but current useItems.ts only has list query. Action mutations may exist in useActions.ts (mark done, snooze) but are item-id based, not action-specific. May need to refactor or add item-level mutations.

decisions.question: What server-side API routes are needed for item actions (snooze, archive, update)?
decisions.answer: Extend existing PATCH /api/items/{item_id} to accept ItemUpdate (priority, status, summary) per api-types.ts. Add POST /api/items/{item_id}/snooze endpoint (accepts hours param, sets snoozed_until). DELETE /api/items/{item_id} already exists for archive per api-types.ts. Mark done via PATCH with status=done. All patterns match existing /api/actions endpoints but operate on any item, not just action items.
decisions.rationale: api-types.ts shows PATCH /api/items/{item_id} and DELETE /api/items/{item_id} already exist. ItemUpdate schema supports priority, status, summary. Snooze pattern exists in /api/actions/{id}/snooze per useActions.ts. Design shows same action bar on search detail as actions page. Just need to expose/create item-level snooze endpoint and connect UI to existing PATCH/DELETE.

decisions.question: How is client-side filtering implemented for kind and text search?
decisions.answer: Client-side filtering in Search.tsx using useMemo: (1) text search via .includes() on summary, id, source, tags array, llm_summary fields (case-insensitive); (2) kind filter via === check on item.kind (all/diff/email/meeting/chat). Filter input is controlled state, auto-focused on mount. Kind filter as button group with active state styling. Pattern matches Triage.tsx filter rail.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype shows client-side filtering (no server round-trip on filter change). Text input + kind buttons. Pattern proven in Triage.tsx which filters client-side on source/priority/time. Search corpus is bounded (recent items, not full archive), so client filtering is performant. Auto-focus pattern from CommandPalette.tsx.

decisions.question: Can we reuse FunnelStage component from filters page (branch 3)?
decisions.answer: Yes, import FunnelStage from page-filters.jsx (branch 3) into Search.tsx. It renders stage timeline with filterId, outcome chip, confidence, reason, context, timing, and correction UI. Search page processing log section uses same component in read-only mode (editable=false). Timing data may not be available in search corpus; handle gracefully with optional timing prop.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype shows identical funnel stage rendering on both Filters page (ItemFunnelDialog) and Search page (processing log card). Component is designed for reuse with editable prop for correction mode. However, branch 3 (filters page) is not yet implemented, so coordination needed. May need to extract FunnelStage to shared components/ if circular dependency issues arise.

decisions.question: How is the search page integrated into the app routing?
decisions.answer: Add to App.tsx Routes: <Route path="/search" element={<Search />} />. Add to AppSidebar.tsx NAV array: { route: '/search', label: 'Search', icon: 'Search', context: 'SEARCH' }. Icon from lucide-react. Position between Overview and Triage in nav order per design shell documentation.
decisions.rationale: Design shell shows /search route with Search icon in nav rail, positioned 2nd (after Overview, before Triage). Current App.tsx routing pattern is straightforward Route elements. NAV array pattern in AppSidebar.tsx matches exactly. All infrastructure exists.

decisions.question: How are action confirmations (done, snooze, archive) communicated to user?
decisions.answer: Use sonner toast (already integrated): import { toast } from 'sonner'. Call toast.success('Item archived') after successful mutation. Pattern matches ActionItems.tsx which shows action feedback. Toast auto-dismisses after 2.2 seconds per design. Error toasts for failed mutations with toast.error().
decisions.rationale: Design prototype shows toast notifications for actions ('Item marked done', 'Snoozed for 4h', etc.). Sonner is already installed and configured in package.json and likely in root provider. Pattern proven in existing pages. Duration 2.2s matches design spec timing for action feedback.

decisions.question: What empty/loading/error states are needed?
decisions.answer: Five states per UI taxonomy: (1) loading: skeleton grid of result rows + detail skeleton; (2) error: alert with message + request ID; (3) unauthorized: full-page lockout (reuse from Overview.tsx); (4) empty: 'No items match filters' with dashed border when filtered, 'Type to search' when no query; (5) no selection: dashed border in right panel 'select an item to inspect its full processing log'.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype defines all five states explicitly. Loading/error/unauthorized/empty pattern is standard across all pages (Overview.tsx, Triage.tsx). No-selection empty state is unique to master/detail layout. All primitives exist (Skeleton, EmptyState, error/unauthorized patterns).

decisions.question: What accessibility considerations are needed for master/detail navigation?
decisions.answer: Master list: role="list" on result container, role="listitem" on ResultRow, aria-label="Search results". Selected row: aria-selected="true", focus management on selection. Detail panel: aria-live="polite" region, aria-labelledby pointing to item ID header. Keyboard nav: arrow keys to move selection, Enter to open (already handled by click), Escape to clear (optional). Search input: aria-label="Search items".
decisions.rationale: Design doesn't explicitly call out a11y but UI taxonomy and existing patterns show consistent a11y. Triage.tsx has keyboard nav (J/K keys). Master/detail is complex interaction requiring ARIA roles. Focus management is critical for screen readers. Pattern should match accessibility-focused component libraries but implementation details need verification.

decisions.question: Are there performance concerns with rich search results?
decisions.answer: Potential concern: search corpus includes full hunks, email bodies, meeting agendas in enriched_context. Mitigations: (1) limit search to recent N items (e.g., 500 most recent) in SQL query; (2) paginate results if count > 100 (offset/limit pattern from Ingestion.tsx jobs table); (3) defer rendering detail panel content until item selected (lazy); (4) use React.memo on ResultRow to prevent re-renders; (5) index summary, tags, llm_summary columns for fast ILIKE.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype shows 8 searchItems in mock data but real corpus could be thousands. Fetching full records with hunks/logs/context for all items is expensive. Current /api/items endpoint supports pagination but hook doesn't use it. Client-side filtering assumes full corpus loaded. Need to balance UX (instant filter) vs performance (paginated API). Trade-offs depend on corpus size.

decisions.question: What is the default state when /search loads with no query?
decisions.answer: Show empty search input (auto-focused), kind filter on 'All', and empty state message 'Type to search across all items'. No API call until query length >= 2 chars (matches command palette MIN_QUERY_LEN pattern). Right panel shows 'select an item' empty state. Alternative: load recent 20 items as starting corpus.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype doesn't show initial state clearly. Command palette waits for 2+ chars before searching. Could apply same pattern (no search = no results) or show recent items by default (discoverability). Empty-first is simpler, matches command palette. Recent-items-first is more useful. Need design decision or user testing.

decisions.question: How is the result count displayed?
decisions.answer: Below search input, mono text: '{count} results' when filtered, hidden when no query. Updates reactively as user types (debounced). Positioned in the header area above the result list, aligned left. Pattern matches Triage.tsx which shows card count.
decisions.rationale: Design prototype shows result count in search header. Common pattern in search UIs. Triage.tsx shows '12 cards' count. Simple derived state from filtered array length. Debouncing matches command palette 200ms pattern to avoid UI flicker during typing.

decisions.question: How is the LLM summary ('Why this matters to you') generated and stored?
decisions.answer: Server-side during item extraction/triage: after priority scoring, call LLM provider with item context + user preference facts to generate personalized summary (2-3 sentences). Store in llm_summary column. Regenerate on preference changes or manual refresh. API: no new endpoint needed, generated as part of item processing pipeline. UI displays read-only with Sparkles icon + 'LLM' label.
decisions.rationale: Design shows LLM summaries as static text with sparkles icon, not editable. Implies server-generated, stored field. Pattern matches existing LLM-scored priority (relevance/urgency). Personalization requires access to user memory/preferences. Regeneration logic (when?) is unclear from design. May need background job or on-demand refresh endpoint.

decisions.question: What new React components are needed for the feedback system?
decisions.answer: 1. FilterTuningCard component (for Actions page) - displays pending tuning tasks with auto-apply/dismiss actions. 2. FunnelStage component (for Filters/Search pages) - vertical timeline stage with correction picker. 3. ItemFunnelDialog component - full per-item provenance view. 4. FilterDetailDialog component - shows items processed by a filter with corrections summary. 5. EnricherDetailDialog component - shows enrichment samples. 6. AddRuleDialog component - create new filter rules. 7. ActionChip component - color-coded filter action indicators. 8. ConfidenceBar component - horizontal progress bar. 9. VerdictPill component - final verdict indicator. 10. FilterRuleCard component - card for filter in ordered funnel. 11. EnricherCard component - card for enricher stage. 12. LoopBackCard component - card for loop-back control stage. 13. SourceChip component - inline source indicator. 14. LiveTail component (for Ingestion page) - auto-scrolling funnel tail. 15. Portal component (shared primitive) - escape overflow/z-index stacking.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype clearly defines each component's purpose, props, and interactions. These components form the complete feedback loop UI: correction capture (FunnelStage), task display (FilterTuningCard), detailed inspection (dialogs), and live monitoring (LiveTail). All follow existing patterns (shadcn/ui composition, TypeScript strict typing, TanStack Query integration).

decisions.question: What new TypeScript types/interfaces are needed?
decisions.answer: 1. FeedbackOverride interface: {id, itemId, itemSummary, filterId, filterPrompt, fromOutcome, fromLabel, toOutcome, toLabel, at}. 2. FilterTuningTask interface: {id, kind: 'filter-tuning', status: 'open'|'applied'|'dismissed', itemId, itemSummary, filterId, filterPrompt, fromOutcome, fromLabel, toOutcome, toLabel, proposedPrompt, at}. 3. FunnelStage interface: {filterId, outcome, confidence, reason, context, weak, timestamp, duration}. 4. FunnelItem interface: extends Item with stages[] array. 5. EnrichmentSample interface: {itemId, summary, contextKV: Record<string,string>, entities: Array}. 6. Enricher interface: {id, sourceType, depth, fields, entities, budget, stats}. 7. LoopBack interface: {id, label, condition, maxLoops, stats}. 8. FilterRuleExtended interface: extends FilterRule with {processed_count, origin: 'learned'|'explicit', match_stats}. 9. PromptPatch type: Map<string, string> (filterId -> refined prompt). 10. Verdict interface: {decision, priority, confidence, rationale, context}.
decisions.rationale: These types directly map to the data structures in the design spec. FeedbackOverride and FilterTuningTask are the core feedback loop types. FunnelStage/FunnelItem support per-item provenance. Enrichment types support the enricher detail views. All types follow existing codebase patterns (Pydantic-like structure, string enums, null safety).

decisions.question: What new API endpoints are needed (server-side)?
decisions.answer: 1. GET /api/feedback/overrides - list all filter corrections. 2. POST /api/feedback/overrides - record a new correction (creates override + tuning task). 3. DELETE /api/feedback/overrides/{itemId}/{filterId} - remove a correction. 4. GET /api/feedback/tasks - list filter-tuning tasks (filtered by status). 5. POST /api/feedback/tasks/{taskId}/apply - apply a prompt patch (writes to filter store). 6. POST /api/feedback/tasks/{taskId}/dismiss - dismiss a tuning task. 7. GET /api/filter-rules/{filterId}/items - items processed by a specific filter. 8. GET /api/items/{itemId}/funnel - full funnel trace for an item. 9. GET /api/enrichers - list all enricher configs. 10. GET /api/enrichers/{enricherId}/samples - enrichment samples for an enricher. 11. GET /api/loopbacks - list loop-back control stages. 12. PATCH /api/filter-rules/{filterId}/prompt - update filter prompt (for manual edits). 13. GET /api/funnel/items - recent items with full funnel traces (for Filters page output table and live tail).
decisions.rationale: The feedback loop requires dedicated endpoints to manage overrides and tasks separately from the existing filter-rules API. The funnel inspection endpoints extend the existing items API with stage-level detail. Enricher/loopback endpoints surface pipeline config that currently lives only in backend domain models. All follow existing REST patterns (GET for reads, POST for writes, PATCH for updates, proper resource nesting).

decisions.question: What new TanStack Query hooks are needed?
decisions.answer: 1. useFeedbackOverrides() - GET /api/feedback/overrides with 30s poll. 2. useAddOverride() - POST mutation, invalidates feedback queries + filter items. 3. useRemoveOverride() - DELETE mutation, invalidates feedback queries. 4. useFeedbackTasks(status?) - GET /api/feedback/tasks?status= with 15s poll. 5. useApplyTask() - POST mutation, invalidates tasks + filter-rules queries. 6. useDismissTask() - POST mutation, invalidates tasks query. 7. useFilterItems(filterId) - GET /api/filter-rules/{filterId}/items, no poll (dialog-only). 8. useItemFunnel(itemId) - GET /api/items/{itemId}/funnel, no poll (dialog-only). 9. useEnrichers() - GET /api/enrichers with 60s poll. 10. useEnricherSamples(enricherId) - GET /api/enrichers/{enricherId}/samples, no poll. 11. useLoopbacks() - GET /api/loopbacks with 60s poll. 12. useFunnelItems(limit?) - GET /api/funnel/items?limit= with 15s poll (live tail). 13. useUpdateFilterPrompt() - PATCH mutation for manual prompt edits. All hooks use pollWhenVisible, follow error-handling patterns from existing hooks (ApiError extraction, toast notifications, optimistic updates where applicable).
decisions.rationale: Each hook maps directly to a new API endpoint or extends existing patterns. Feedback hooks need polling for live task updates. Dialog-only hooks (filter items, item funnel, enricher samples) should not poll to reduce server load. Mutations follow existing patterns (invalidate related queries, toast on success/error). The useFeedbackStore client-only hook complements these by managing prompt patches in React state.

decisions.question: What existing components need modification?
decisions.answer: 1. ActionItems.tsx - add FilterTuning section above throughput chart, render FilterTuningCard for open tasks. 2. Ingestion.tsx - add LiveTail component at top, embed IngestionFunnel component at bottom. 3. pages/Filters.tsx - NEW page (FiltersPage component) to replace existing filter management, becomes primary funnel config surface. 4. pages/Search.tsx - NEW page (SearchPage component) with master/detail layout, ItemFunnelDialog integration. 5. App.tsx/Router - add /filters and /search routes. 6. AppSidebar.tsx - add nav items for Filters (Workflow icon) and Search (Search icon). 7. primitives.jsx (if using design prototype pattern) - add Portal, useFeedbackStore hook. No modifications to existing StatCard, Sparkline, DataTable, ChartCard, etc. - these remain unchanged.
decisions.rationale: The design spec explicitly calls out modifications to ActionItems (filter tuning section) and Ingestion (live tail + embedded funnel). Filters and Search are net-new pages, not modifications. The router and sidebar changes are straightforward additions. Existing display primitives are stable and reused as-is. The feedback store is a new client-side singleton, not a modification to existing hooks.

decisions.question: What testing strategy is needed?
decisions.answer: 1. Unit tests for feedback store (WBFeedback): addOverride creates task + refines prompt, removeOverride clears task, autoApply updates promptPatches, promptFor returns patched prompt with fallback. 2. Component tests for FilterTuningCard: renders task details, auto-apply calls mutation, dismiss calls mutation. 3. Component tests for FunnelStage: renders stage details, correction picker opens on 'correct' click, correction submission calls addOverride. 4. Integration tests for ItemFunnelDialog: renders all stages, shows corrected outcomes with strikethrough, timing calculations are correct. 5. MSW mocks for new endpoints: /api/feedback/*, /api/filter-rules/{id}/items, /api/items/{id}/funnel, /api/enrichers, /api/loopbacks, /api/funnel/items. 6. E2E test for full feedback loop: correct a filter classification -> task appears on Actions page -> auto-apply -> prompt updates on Filters page. 7. Accessibility tests: FunnelStage correction picker keyboard nav, FilterTuningCard focus management, dialogs aria-labelledby/describedby. Follow existing patterns from ActionItems.test.tsx, Triage.test.tsx (React Testing Library + Vitest + MSW).
decisions.rationale: Testing strategy follows existing codebase patterns (unit tests for stores/hooks, component tests for UI, MSW for API mocking). The feedback loop introduces complex state dependencies (corrections -> tasks -> prompt patches) that require integration testing. E2E coverage ensures the full loop works. Medium confidence because the design spec doesn't specify testing requirements, but the existing codebase has comprehensive test coverage (*.test.tsx for every page/component) that should be matched.

decisions.question: What accessibility considerations are needed?
decisions.answer: 1. FunnelStage correction picker: keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow keys, Enter to select), aria-expanded on 'correct' button, role='group' on picker, aria-label on outcome choices. 2. FilterTuningCard: semantic heading (h3) for filter ID, clear button labels ('Auto-apply update', 'I'll do it manually'), focus management after dismiss (return to next task or containing section). 3. ItemFunnelDialog: aria-labelledby pointing to item ID heading, aria-describedby for summary, scrollable region has aria-label='Funnel stages', FunnelStage list as ordered list (ol) with proper nesting. 4. FilterDetailDialog: table of processed items has proper th/td structure, aria-sort on sortable columns if added later, click-to-open-funnel pattern needs Enter key support + aria-label. 5. LiveTail: role='log' + aria-live='polite' on scrollable region (already follows LogStream pattern), aria-label='Live funnel tail', row selection via keyboard (arrow keys + Enter). 6. ActionChip/VerdictPill: ensure sufficient contrast for all states (green/orange/red/cyan on dark background), test against WCAG AA. 7. ConfidenceBar: aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax attributes, visible percentage label for screen readers. All dialogs must have Escape-to-close + focus trap (follow existing Dialog primitive pattern). Ensure Portal-rendered content is in DOM order for screen readers.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype doesn't explicitly document a11y, but the existing codebase has strong accessibility patterns (LogStream uses role='log'/aria-live, CommandPalette has keyboard nav, Topology has visually-hidden fallback table). The new components introduce interactive pickers and data visualizations that need proper ARIA semantics. ADR 0046 enforces contrast standards. The correction picker is the highest-risk a11y surface (nested interactive elements, state changes) and needs careful testing.

decisions.question: What performance concerns need to be addressed?
decisions.answer: 1. LiveTail streaming: cap at 60 rows max (spec says this), use virtualization if pool exceeds 500 items (react-window or manual windowing). 2. ItemFunnelDialog stage rendering: memoize FunnelStage components (React.memo) to prevent re-renders when dialog scrolls, compute timings once in useMemo. 3. Filters page reordering: optimistic UI update + debounced PATCH to avoid race conditions, use CSS transitions instead of re-rendering full list. 4. useFeedbackStore subscription: ensure subscribers are unsubscribed on unmount to prevent memory leaks, use shallow equality check to avoid unnecessary re-renders. 5. FilterDetailDialog items table: paginate if >100 items, lazy-load item funnels only when row is clicked (not on table mount). 6. Search page master/detail: virtualize result list if >50 items (lucide Search icon), debounce search input (200ms, already standard in CommandPalette). 7. Prompt patch diffing: cache refinedPrompt() result per override, don't recompute on every render. 8. Feedback task polling: use pollWhenVisible(15000) to pause when tab hidden, consider WebSocket for real-time updates if >10 concurrent users (unlikely for single-user tool). 9. Enrichment samples: limit to 3 samples per enricher in detail dialog to keep payload small. 10. Chart re-renders: MultiLineChart and SourceFlow use requestAnimationFrame for animations - ensure cleanup on unmount.
decisions.rationale: Most performance concerns are addressed by existing patterns (TanStack Query caching, pollWhenVisible, React.memo). LiveTail is the highest-risk surface (streaming data, DOM churn) but spec already caps it at 60 rows. The feedback store is client-only and manages small datasets (typically <20 overrides, <10 tasks). Search page virtualization is only needed if corpus grows >1000 items (unlikely for single-user). Medium confidence because actual performance depends on real-world usage patterns not fully specified in design.

decisions.question: What is the feedback store architecture and persistence strategy?
decisions.answer: Client-side only. WBFeedback is a module-scoped singleton (like existing api.ts token cache pattern). State: {overrides[], tasks[], promptPatches: Map<filterId, string>}. Persistence: localStorage with key 'workbench.feedback', serialize/deserialize on load/change. Sync across tabs via storage event listener (like useWorkMode pattern). Server integration: overrides/tasks read from /api/feedback/* on mount to seed initial state, then kept in sync via mutations. promptPatches are local-only until auto-applied (POST /api/feedback/tasks/{id}/apply writes to server). No optimistic updates for corrections - wait for server confirmation to avoid race conditions. Subscribe/notify pattern for React integration: useFeedbackStore() hook subscribes on mount, unsubscribes on unmount, forces re-render on any state change. Exposed globally on window.WBFeedback for debugging (follows existing window.WB pattern from design prototype). Fallback: if localStorage unavailable (privacy mode), fall back to in-memory only with warning toast on first correction.
decisions.rationale: The design spec describes WBFeedback as a 'global singleton' with subscribe/notify pattern and local promptPatches cache, which maps to module-scoped + localStorage. The existing codebase has precedent for client-side singletons (api.ts token cache) and localStorage sync (useWorkMode). However, the spec doesn't explicitly detail persistence or cross-tab sync, so medium confidence. Server-first alternative (store everything server-side) would be simpler but requires more backend work and loses the 'instant prompt preview' UX benefit.

decisions.question: How should the funnel evaluation order (enrichers, filters, loop-backs) be stored and updated?
decisions.answer: Single unified ordering array stored server-side: [{kind: 'enricher'|'filter'|'loopback', id: string, order: number}]. Endpoint: GET /api/funnel/order returns ordered list, PATCH /api/funnel/order {items: [{kind, id, order}]} updates. Client-side: Filters page maintains order state as array, optimistic reorder on up/down arrow click (swap adjacent items), debounced PATCH after 500ms idle. Backend: funnel/order config stored in new funnel_stages table (schema: id, kind, stage_id, order, enabled). Pipeline engine reads this order at runtime to determine execution sequence. Enrichers run first for their target source_type, then filters for that source, then loop-backs can re-inject. Stage execution: pipeline/engine.py loads ordered stages, groups by source_type, executes sequentially per item. Enable/disable: PATCH /api/funnel/stages/{id} {enabled: bool} toggles without reordering. Default order on fresh install: all enrichers (by source_type alpha), then all filters (by created_at), then loop-backs. Move operation: swap order values of two adjacent stages, backend validates no gaps in sequence.
decisions.rationale: The design spec shows a unified interleaved order with up/down arrows, implying a single sequence. The 'enrichers, filters, loop-backs in a single reorderable list' pattern requires server-side storage of the ordering. However, the spec doesn't detail the backend schema or API contract. Medium confidence because this is a reasonable extension of existing patterns (filter-rules store, source configs) but requires new storage layer. Alternative: client-only ordering would be simpler but lose persistence across sessions.

decisions.question: What is the scope of the initial implementation vs future branches?
decisions.answer: Initial (this branch): 1. Feedback store (WBFeedback) with override/task management, promptFor() API, localStorage persistence. 2. FilterTuningCard on Actions page. 3. FunnelStage with correction picker. 4. ItemFunnelDialog with full trace + timing. 5. New API endpoints: /api/feedback/*, /api/items/{id}/funnel, /api/filter-rules/{id}/items. 6. New hooks: useFeedbackOverrides, useAddOverride, useFeedbackTasks, useApplyTask, useDismissTask, useItemFunnel, useFilterItems. 7. ActionItems page modifications (filter tuning section). 8. Ingestion page LiveTail (without full Filters page). 9. Basic tests for feedback store + FilterTuningCard + FunnelStage. Future branches: 1. Full Filters page (FiltersPage component) with enricher/filter/loopback cards, reordering, detail dialogs. 2. Search page with master/detail layout. 3. Enricher/loopback config endpoints + hooks. 4. SourceFlow Sankey visualization (complex animation, separate branch). 5. MultiLineChart component (if not already built). 6. EnricherDetailDialog, FilterDetailDialog (depend on full Filters page). 7.
