The feedback loop (override -> task -> prompt patch) is the core value and can be delivered incrementally. The LiveTail is a natural extension of existing Ingestion page. The full Filters page is substantial (9 sub-components, reordering UX, 3 detail dialogs) and should be a separate branch. This scoping follows the 'small, testable, shippable increments' principle and allows validating the feedback UX before building the full funnel config surface.

decisions.question: What new React component is needed for the animated Sankey flow visualization?
decisions.answer: Create src/components/SourceFlow.tsx as a TypeScript port of the prototype's SourceFlow component. It will render an animated SVG Sankey diagram showing source→WorkBench→output flows with: (1) Bézier ribbon paths connecting source/output nodes through a central bar, (2) requestAnimationFrame-driven animated dots flowing along ribbons (density proportional to flow volume), (3) stalled source detection (red dashed ribbons + alert icon when health_status === 'erroring'), (4) hover isolation with smooth re-proportioning (hovering a source re-proportions outputs; hovering an output re-proportions inputs), (5) click navigation for output nodes. Use React.useState for focus state, React.useMemo for layout computation, React.useRef for path/dot element refs, React.useEffect for rAF animation loop cleanup. Import lucide-react icons (Github, Mail, Calendar, MessageCircle, CircleCheckBig, ListChecks, Filter, TriangleAlert, ArrowDownToLine, ArrowUpFromLine). Component accepts onNavigate callback prop for routing to clicked outputs.
decisions.rationale: The prototype shows a complete, self-contained SourceFlow component with well-defined props and internal state. The existing codebase uses TypeScript + React 19 + lucide-react icons. The pattern matches other chart components (Topology.tsx): hand-rolled SVG with role='img', accessibility labels, and smooth CSS transitions. The animation loop is rAF-based (no library), which is appropriate for 60fps smooth flow. This is a new visualization type not present in the current codebase.

decisions.question: What new TypeScript types/interfaces are needed for SourceFlow?
decisions.answer: No new exported interfaces required. SourceFlow will use inline types for its internal SOURCES/OUTPUTS/M matrix data structures and consume the existing SourceRollup[] type from useStats.ts (which already has health_status field). The component will read window.WB.sources (prototype pattern) OR accept sources prop typed as SourceRollup[] for production. Focus state type will be inline: { t: 'none' | 'src' | 'out', i: number, j: number }. Ribbon metadata will be inline: { side: 'L' | 'R', idx: number, color: string, value: number, on: boolean, broken: boolean, band: string, mid: string }.
decisions.rationale: The existing SourceRollup interface already includes health_status ('disabled' | 'never_run' | 'erroring' | 'healthy') which is exactly what SourceFlow needs to detect stalled sources. The prototype uses window.WB.sources which maps to this type. No new backend API types needed since /api/stats/sources already returns the required data. Internal component types can be inline since they're implementation details, following the pattern in Topology.tsx which also uses inline types for layout positions.

decisions.question: What new API endpoints are needed on the server side?
decisions.answer: No new API endpoints required. SourceFlow will consume the existing GET /api/stats/sources endpoint (already polled by useSourcesRollup hook) which returns SourceRollup[] with health_status. The flow matrix M[source][output] and volume calculations will be computed client-side from aggregated stats already available in StatsOverview (useStatsOverview hook returns items.by_source breakdown). Output node volumes (Action Items count, Triage Queue count, etc.) are derived from existing overview stats (pending_triage, active_items) and queue stats (by_status). All necessary data already flows through the UI's existing API contract.
decisions.rationale: The prototype hardcodes the flow matrix M and volumes as mock data. In production, these can be derived from existing API responses: (1) source volumes from SourceRollup.items_stored, (2) output volumes from StatsOverview (pending_triage for Triage Queue, active_items for Action Items) and QueueStats.by_status (filtered/dropped counts), (3) flow proportions computed client-side using the same breakdown ratios. The health_status field for stalled-source detection already exists in /api/stats/sources. No new backend computation needed—this is a pure visualization layer concern.

decisions.question: What new TanStack Query hooks are needed?
decisions.answer: No new hooks required. SourceFlow will consume three existing hooks: (1) useSourcesRollup() for source health status and volumes, (2) useStatsOverview() for output node volumes (pending_triage, active_items, items.by_status breakdown), (3) useQueueStats() for filtered/error counts. These are already polled at appropriate intervals (30s/15s/15s). The component will destructure data from these hooks in its parent container (likely Overview page) and pass computed props, OR consume the hooks directly if used as a standalone widget.
decisions.rationale: All three hooks already exist and are used extensively across pages. useSourcesRollup returns SourceRollup[] with health_status (stalled detection). useStatsOverview returns ItemsBreakdown.by_source (for source volumes) and counts for outputs. useQueueStats provides queue depth by status (for Filtered Out / Errors buckets). The polling intervals are already appropriate for live monitoring. No new data fetching patterns needed—this follows the established pattern where chart components receive pre-fetched data as props (see Topology component which receives Topology object from useTopology hook).

decisions.question: What existing components need modification?
decisions.answer: Minimal modifications: (1) Add SourceFlow to Overview.tsx as a new card in the Infrastructure section (replace or augment the existing Topology graph). Import SourceFlow component, consume useSourcesRollup + useStatsOverview + useQueueStats hooks, compute flow matrix from stats, render <SourceFlow sources={sources} flows={flowMatrix} onNavigate={navigate} />. (2) Export SourceFlow from src/components/index.ts (if using barrel exports). (3) Optionally create a ChartCard variant or use existing Card wrapper for consistent styling. No modifications to hooks, API layer, or other pages required.
decisions.rationale: The prototype shows SourceFlow as a standalone visualization that could replace or complement the existing Topology graph on the Overview page. The existing Topology component uses similar patterns (pure SVG, role='img', accessibility). Integration is straightforward: add the component, wire up data from existing hooks, pass onNavigate callback. Medium confidence because the exact placement strategy (replace Topology vs. separate card vs. tabbed view) is a UX decision not fully specified in the branch description. The component itself is self-contained and doesn't require modifications to other components.

decisions.question: What testing strategy is appropriate for SourceFlow?
decisions.answer: Three-tier strategy: (1) Unit tests (SourceFlow.test.tsx) using @testing-library/react + Vitest: test layout computation logic (ribbon path generation, node positioning, re-proportioning on hover), verify focus state transitions, check stalled source rendering (red ribbons when health_status='erroring'), assert aria-label presence. Mock the rAF animation loop. (2) Visual regression (optional): screenshot tests for hover states and stalled indicators. (3) Integration test: render with real hook data mocks (MSW handlers for /api/stats/sources), verify click navigation callback, test keyboard navigation if added. Follow existing test patterns from Topology.test.tsx (SVG structure assertions, accessibility checks).
decisions.rationale: The component has three testable concerns: (1) layout math (ribbon paths, node positions, proportioning), (2) interaction state (hover focus, click navigation), (3) stalled source detection. The rAF animation is hard to test in JSDOM but can be mocked/skipped. Existing codebase has comprehensive component tests (see Topology, Sparkline tests) using @testing-library/react + Vitest. The accessibility requirement (aria-label, role='img') mirrors Topology's pattern. Medium confidence because animation testing can be flaky; may need snapshot tests or visual regression tools beyond the current test stack.

decisions.question: What are the key accessibility considerations for SourceFlow?
decisions.answer: Five requirements: (1) Add role='img' and comprehensive aria-label summarizing the flow (e.g., 'Signal flow: 612 items/day from github, 388 from email... to 280 Action Items, 410 Triage Queue, 540 Filtered Out, 54 Errors. Hover a source or output to see breakdown.'). (2) Provide a visually-hidden <table> fallback (sr-only class) listing all flows in tabular format (Source | Volume | Destination | Count), mirroring Topology.tsx pattern. (3) Ensure output nodes are keyboard-navigable buttons (not just click handlers on SVG elements) with visible focus rings. (4) Add title elements to each source/output node for tooltip-style descriptions. (5) Respect prefers-reduced-motion: disable rAF animation loop and CSS transitions when user has motion sensitivity. Use media query in useEffect cleanup.
decisions.rationale: The existing Topology component sets the precedent: role='img', aria-label summary, plus a visually-hidden <table> fallback for screen readers. This is the correct pattern per WCAG 2.2 for complex SVG visualizations. The prototype's click handlers on output nodes need to be keyboard-accessible (use foreignObject with button elements or add keyboard event handlers). Motion reduction is critical for animated visualizations—other components (Sparkline, transitions) already respect prefers-reduced-motion via CSS. The component description explicitly mentions accessibility as a key consideration, and the settled ADRs emphasize contrast/focus rings.

decisions.question: What are the performance concerns and mitigation strategies?
decisions.answer: Four concerns + mitigations: (1) rAF animation loop: Limit dot pool size (80 dots in prototype). Use requestAnimationFrame with delta-time throttling. Clean up rAF on unmount and when tab is hidden (check document.visibilityState). (2) Layout recomputation on hover: Memoize layout calculations with React.useMemo keyed on focus state. Avoid recomputing ribbon paths when only opacity changes. (3) SVG re-renders: Use React.memo on the component if it's re-rendered frequently by parent. Cache path refs in React.useRef to avoid getTotalLength() calls every frame. (4) Large flow matrices: Keep matrix size small (4 sources × 4 outputs = 16 flows max). If sources grow beyond ~10, consider aggregating or paginating. Monitor paint time with React DevTools Profiler.
decisions.rationale: The prototype's rAF loop is well-designed: it uses delta-time for frame-rate independence, limits the dot pool to 80, and spawns dots proportionally to flow volume. The main risk is unnecessary layout thrashing on hover. React.useMemo on the layout object (keyed on focus.t/focus.i/focus.j) prevents recomputation except when focus changes. Path.getTotalLength() is expensive but cached in refs and called only on layout change. Medium confidence because real-world performance depends on browser SVG rendering speed and the number of concurrent transitions. May need to profile with Chrome DevTools Performance tab on lower-end devices. The codebase's existing charts are lightweight, so this shouldn't introduce major perf regressions.

decisions.question: How should SourceFlow integrate with the existing centralized chart theme?
decisions.answer: Import CHART_COLORS and CHART_PALETTE from @/lib/chart-theme.ts. Use CHART_COLORS.primary (#ff6a2b) for github source, CHART_COLORS.tertiary (#71d2ff) for email, CHART_COLORS.amber (#ffb59a) for calendar, CHART_COLORS.green (#9ad08a) for chat. Use error color #e5484d for stalled source ribbons (not in CHART_COLORS but consistent with destructive variant). Output colors can use extended palette or semantic colors (Action Items: purple #b79cf7, Triage Queue: #9a7af0, Filtered: gray #71717a, Errors: red #e5484d). Grid lines and borders use CHART_DEFAULTS.grid.stroke (#26262C). Define a local SOURCEFLOW_COLORS constant for output node colors to avoid hardcoding, but source colors should map to CHART_PALETTE for consistency with other multi-series charts.
decisions.rationale: ADR 0038 mandates centralized chart theming to prevent color drift. The prototype hardcodes hex values that closely match CHART_COLORS (primary/tertiary/amber/green). Importing from chart-theme.ts ensures future theme changes (e.g., light mode support, accessibility contrast tuning) apply to SourceFlow automatically. The error red for stalled sources is a semantic color (destructive state) and should remain distinct. Output node colors are domain-specific (Action Items, Triage Queue) and can be local constants, but they should still respect the overall palette harmony. This follows the pattern in BarChart (Overview.tsx) which uses CHART_COLORS for priority-based fills.

decisions.question: How should stalled source indicators be implemented and surfaced?
decisions.answer: Three-part implementation: (1) Detect stalled sources by filtering sources.filter(s => s.health_status === 'erroring'). Store in a Set for O(1) lookup. (2) Visual treatment: render stalled source node with fill='#e5484d' (error red), ribbon with stroke='#e5484d', strokeDasharray='5 3', strokeOpacity='0.6', and fillOpacity reduced to 0.12. Add a TriangleAlert icon (lucide-react) next to the source label. Replace volume text with 'STALLED' label in uppercase mono font. (3) Hover behavior: when hovering a stalled source, zero out the right-side (output) proportions to visually indicate no flow. Add a tooltip (foreignObject <title>) explaining 'Ingestion stalled — check source configuration'. Cross-reference the Sources page health badge pattern for visual consistency.
decisions.rationale: The prototype shows clear stalled-source handling: red dashed ribbons, triangle alert icon, 'stalled' label instead of volume. This maps directly to SourceRollup.health_status === 'erroring' from the existing API. The visual treatment is consistent with error states elsewhere (red destructive variant, dashed borders for warnings). Zeroing outputs on hover makes logical sense: a stalled source produces zero flow. The HealthBadge component already renders 'erroring' status with red styling, so this is an extension of that pattern to the flow diagram. High confidence because the API contract is already stable and the visual design is fully specified in the prototype.

decisions.question: What tabs primitive should we use for the Settings sub-tab navigation?
decisions.answer: Implement Radix UI Tabs primitive following shadcn/ui pattern (components/ui/tabs.tsx). This matches the existing design system stack and provides accessible tab navigation. The component should export: Tabs (root), TabsList (horizontal flex container), TabsTrigger (individual tab button), TabsContent (panel wrapper). Styling should match the prototype: role='tablist', bottom border on TabsList, 2px solid --primary bottom border on active tab with negative margin trick to overlap tablist border, text-muted-foreground inactive state, text-foreground active state.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype explicitly describes a tab pattern with role='tablist' and aria-selected. Radix UI Tabs is the standard primitive for this in the shadcn/ui stack already used throughout the codebase. This provides keyboard navigation (arrow keys), ARIA attributes, and controlled/uncontrolled modes out of the box. The visual styling described in the prototype (bottom border, overlap trick) is standard and tested.

decisions.question: Should Settings sub-tabs use React Router sub-routes or controlled tab state?
decisions.answer: Use React Router sub-routes with URL-driven tab state: /settings (defaults to System tab), /settings/sources (Sources tab), /settings/messenger (Messenger tab). The active tab is derived from route.pathname parsing: pathname.split('/')[2] with fallback to 'system'. Clicking a tab navigates via <Link> or navigate() rather than controlled tab state. This makes sub-tabs bookmarkable, preserves browser back/forward, and aligns with the existing routing pattern.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype explicitly shows this pattern: 'Active tab derived from route: /settings -> "system", /settings/sources -> "sources"'. The existing App.tsx uses React Router v7. URL-driven tabs are the standard pattern for multi-page dashboards and align with user expectations (bookmarkable, back button works). The prototype's SettingsPage already demonstrates the route parsing logic.

decisions.question: How should we refactor Settings.tsx to support the tab container pattern?
decisions.answer: Refactor Settings.tsx to be a container with three sections: (1) Page header with h1 'Settings', (2) Tabs navigation bar using the new Tabs primitive with three TabsTrigger components (System/Sources/Messenger with icons), (3) Content area that renders the active tab component based on route. Move current Settings.tsx content into a new SettingsSystem component. Render <Outlet /> from React Router to display the child route components (SettingsSystem at index route, Sources at /sources child route, Messenger at /messenger child route). Alternatively, use conditional rendering if not using nested routes.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype shows two possible architectures: (a) conditional rendering based on parsed route, (b) nested routes with Outlet. The prototype uses conditional rendering which is simpler and already works in the hash-based environment. However, React Router v7 supports nested routes which would be cleaner. Given the existing codebase uses flat routes and the prototype pattern is already proven, conditional rendering is safer and requires fewer routing changes.

decisions.question: Should we use the 'embedded' prop pattern for Sources and Messenger pages or create separate components?
decisions.answer: Use the embedded prop pattern: add an optional 'embedded?: boolean' prop to Sources.tsx and Messenger.tsx. When embedded=true, hide the page-level h1 title and any redundant chrome, since the Settings container provides the title and tab navigation. This allows reuse of the same component at both /sources (standalone) and /settings/sources (embedded in tab). The prop controls only presentational concerns (title visibility), not data fetching or business logic.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype explicitly describes this pattern: 'The "embedded" prop allows SourcesPage and MessengerPage to be used both standalone (at /sources, /messenger) and embedded within the settings tabs. This is a reuse pattern -- the same page components serve two contexts.' This avoids code duplication while supporting both navigation patterns. The current Sources.tsx and Messenger.tsx already have self-contained h1 titles that can be conditionally rendered.

decisions.question: What changes to App.tsx routing are needed?
decisions.answer: Add nested routes under /settings: <Route path='/settings' element={<Settings />}><Route index element={<SettingsSystem />} /><Route path='sources' element={<Sources embedded />} /><Route path='messenger' element={<Messenger embedded />} /></Route>. Keep the existing standalone routes /sources and /messenger for backward compatibility and direct navigation. The Settings component renders <Outlet /> to display the child route. If nested routes prove complex with HashRouter, use the conditional rendering pattern from the prototype instead.
decisions.rationale: React Router v7 supports nested routes but the existing codebase uses flat routes. The prototype shows conditional rendering which is simpler but less idiomatic. Nested routes provide better separation of concerns and follow React Router conventions. The risk is complexity with the HashRouter + nested routes interaction. Fallback: conditional rendering as shown in prototype is proven to work.

decisions.question: Should the sidebar Settings nav item link to /settings or /settings/system?
decisions.answer: Link to /settings (no sub-path). The Settings page index route defaults to the System tab. This provides the cleanest URL and follows the principle that /settings is the canonical entry point, with sub-tabs as refinements. The NavLink in AppSidebar.tsx remains { to: '/settings', label: 'Settings', icon: Settings }.
decisions.rationale: Standard navigation pattern: the primary nav goes to the top-level route, which then provides sub-navigation. The /settings route will render the Settings container with the System tab active by default (either via index route or fallback logic). This keeps URLs clean and predictable.

decisions.question: What new React components need to be created?
decisions.answer: 1. components/ui/tabs.tsx - Radix UI Tabs primitive wrapper (Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent) following shadcn/ui pattern. 2. pages/SettingsSystem.tsx - Extract current Settings.tsx content (versions, health, config sections, secrets vault, download backup) into this new component. This becomes the System tab content. No other new page components needed since Sources and Messenger already exist.
decisions.rationale: The tabs primitive is the only missing UI component from the design system. The SettingsSystem component is a straightforward extraction of existing code from Settings.tsx. Sources and Messenger pages already exist and just need the embedded prop added. This is the minimal set of new components required.

decisions.question: What new TypeScript types/interfaces are needed?
decisions.answer: No new API types needed - all data shapes already exist (HealthResponse, DebugConfigResponse, MessengerInfo, SourceRollup). Only presentational types: (1) Add 'embedded?: boolean' to Sources and Messenger component props (inline prop typing is sufficient). (2) TabValue type alias: type TabValue = 'system' | 'sources' | 'messenger' for type safety in route parsing and tab state (optional but recommended).
decisions.rationale: This is purely a UI reorganization. All data types already exist in the current pages. The embedded prop is a simple boolean presentational flag. A TabValue union type provides type safety for the route parsing logic but is not strictly required.

decisions.question: What new API endpoints are needed?
decisions.answer: No new API endpoints required. All three tabs use existing endpoints: System tab uses GET /health and GET /api/debug/config (already in useSettings.ts hooks). Sources tab uses GET /api/stats/sources and source mutation endpoints (already in useSources.ts). Messenger tab uses GET /api/messenger and PATCH /api/messenger (already in useMessenger.ts). This is purely a client-side UI reorganization.
decisions.rationale: The design spec confirms this is a consolidation/reorganization of existing pages under a tab interface. No new data is being displayed, just existing pages being embedded in a new navigation structure. All hooks and endpoints are already implemented and tested.

decisions.question: What new TanStack Query hooks are needed?
decisions.answer: No new hooks required. All data fetching hooks already exist: useHealth() and useDebugConfig() from hooks/useSettings.ts for System tab. useSourceStats(), useToggleSource(), usePollSource(), useDeleteSource() from hooks/useSources.ts for Sources tab. useMessenger(), usePendingCount(), useUpdateMessenger() from hooks/useMessenger.ts for Messenger tab. The embedded prop is purely presentational and doesn't affect data fetching.
decisions.rationale: The existing pages are fully functional with their own data fetching. The tab structure doesn't change what data is fetched, only how the pages are organized visually. Each tab continues to use its existing hooks. No data sharing between tabs is required.

decisions.question: What testing strategy should we use for the new tab structure?
decisions.answer: 1. Unit test components/ui/tabs.tsx: verify Radix Tabs wrapper passes through props, applies className, renders children. 2. Update Settings.test.tsx: test tab navigation (clicking tab triggers navigate), test route-driven active state (url /settings shows System active, /settings/sources shows Sources active), test that all three tab panels render when active. 3. Add embedded prop tests to Sources.test.tsx and Messenger.test.tsx: verify h1 is hidden when embedded=true, shown when embedded=false/undefined. 4. Integration test: verify standalone routes /sources and /messenger still work. Use existing MSW mocks. Follow existing test patterns (Vitest + Testing Library).
decisions.rationale: The existing codebase has comprehensive tests for all three pages. The testing additions are incremental: test the new tabs primitive, test the tab navigation/routing logic, test the embedded prop presentational changes. The MSW server is already set up with all necessary endpoint mocks. This follows the established testing patterns in the codebase.

decisions.question: What accessibility considerations are needed for the tab structure?
decisions.answer: 1. Radix UI Tabs provides accessible tab pattern out of the box: role='tablist' on container, role='tab' on triggers, role='tabpanel' on content, aria-selected on active tab, aria-controls/aria-labelledby associations, keyboard navigation (Arrow keys, Home, End). 2. Ensure TabsTrigger includes both icon and label text (not icon-only) for screen readers. 3. The existing a11y.test.tsx should be updated to verify the Settings route has proper tab ARIA attributes. 4. Preserve focus management: when navigating to a tab via URL (not click), focus should move to the active tab panel heading. 5. Ensure focus-visible ring styles from index.css apply to TabsTrigger elements.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype explicitly mentions role='tablist' and aria-selected. Radix UI Tabs is WCAG 2.1 compliant and handles the complex ARIA patterns. The existing codebase has strong a11y practices (a11y.test.tsx, focus-visible styles). The main concern is ensuring tab triggers have visible labels (not just icons) and that focus management works with URL-driven navigation.

decisions.question: Are there any performance concerns with the tab structure?
decisions.answer: No significant performance concerns. Each tab component only mounts when active (TabsContent renders children conditionally). Data fetching hooks use TanStack Query with staleTime/polling, so switching tabs may trigger refetches but this is intended behavior. Potential optimization: if switching between tabs causes jank, consider keeping inactive tab components mounted but hidden (aria-hidden) to preserve query cache. However, start with unmount-on-hide (default Radix behavior) as it's simpler and follows the prototype pattern. The existing pages have no performance issues, so tab wrapping shouldn't introduce new problems.
decisions.rationale: The tab structure is lightweight (just conditional rendering). Each tab uses the same hooks it uses now as a standalone page, so no new performance characteristics. TanStack Query handles caching and background refetching. The only risk is if users rapidly switch tabs and trigger many refetches, but this is unlikely and the hooks already have staleTime configuration. The prototype doesn't mention performance optimizations, suggesting the default behavior is acceptable.

decisions.question: Should tab triggers include icons alongside labels?
decisions.answer: Yes, include lucide-react icons in each TabsTrigger: System tab uses SlidersHorizontal icon, Sources tab uses Database icon, Messenger tab uses MessageSquare icon (as specified in the prototype TABS array). Render icon + label together inside each trigger, following the pattern: {label}. This matches the design prototype and provides visual wayfinding while keeping labels for accessibility.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype explicitly specifies icons for each tab: 'Three tabs defined in TABS array: System (SlidersHorizontal icon), Sources (Database icon), Messenger (MessageSquare icon).' Icons improve scannability and visual hierarchy. The aria-hidden on icons ensures screen readers focus on the label text. This follows the same pattern used in AppSidebar.tsx.

decisions.question: Should we maintain the standalone /sources and /messenger routes or deprecate them?
decisions.answer: Maintain both standalone routes /sources and /messenger AND the embedded tab routes /settings/sources and /settings/messenger. The standalone routes render the full page with h1 title (embedded=false). This provides flexibility: users can link directly to Sources or Messenger without going through Settings, while the Settings tabs provide grouped navigation for related configuration. Update AppSidebar.tsx to keep Sources and Messenger nav items, or remove them if consolidating all config under Settings. Recommend: remove Sources and Messenger from sidebar (they're now sub-tabs of Settings) but keep the routes active for direct links and backward compatibility.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype mentions 'legacy/alias routes' and shows both patterns. Removing the standalone routes would break existing links/bookmarks. Keeping them provides flexibility at minimal cost (just a boolean prop). The design question is whether to keep them in the sidebar nav. The prototype suggests removing them from primary nav since Settings consolidates all configuration, but keeping the routes themselves active is low-risk and user-friendly.

decisions.question: Should Sources and Messenger nav items be removed from AppSidebar.tsx?
decisions.answer: Remove Sources and Messenger from the primary AppSidebar nav. They become sub-tabs under Settings only. This reduces visual clutter in the icon rail and provides a clearer information architecture: Settings is the single entry point for all configuration (System/Sources/Messenger). The NAV array in AppSidebar.tsx should be updated to remove the Database and MessageSquare entries. Users access these via Settings > [Sources|Messenger] tab. Direct URL access to /sources and /messenger still works for deep links.
decisions.rationale: The branch name is 'Settings sub-tabs: System/Sources/Messenger consolidation' which implies bringing Sources and Messenger under Settings rather than having them in parallel. The prototype describes Settings as 'the container' with sub-tabs. Removing from sidebar simplifies navigation. However, this is a UX trade-off: some users may prefer Sources/Messenger as top-level items. Recommend: start with removal (consolidation), can always add back if user testing shows strong preference for top-level access.

decisions.question: What new React components are needed for the hover-expand rail?
decisions.answer: No new components needed. The existing AppSidebar.tsx already implements a similar pattern but needs CSS updates to support hover-expand. The component structure is correct - it renders nav items with icons and labels. The CSS needs to add hover transitions (width 64px → 216px, label opacity 0 → 1, box-shadow on hover) mirroring the design prototype's wb-rail-nav behavior in app.css lines 25-59.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype shows the hover-expand is purely CSS-driven (transition on width, opacity, box-shadow). The existing AppSidebar already has the correct DOM structure with NavLink items containing icons and labels. We just need to update the Tailwind classes or add custom CSS to match the prototype's hover behavior.

decisions.question: Does the rail need a logo/brand mark at the top?
decisions.answer: Yes. Add a logo button at the top of AppSidebar that shows the WB icon (34x34) and 'WorkBench' label (display font, weight 600). This button should navigate to / when clicked. The design prototype shows this in shell.jsx lines 37-40 with className 'wb-rail-logo' that gets margin-bottom: 12px.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype explicitly shows a wb-rail-logo button as the first item in the rail (shell.jsx line 37-40) with the WB icon and WorkBench label. The existing codebase's AppSidebar does not have this - it only shows nav items. The TopBar has a brand mark but the rail needs its own for consistency when hovering.

decisions.question: What navigation items should appear in the rail after adding Search and removing Sources/Messenger?
decisions.answer: The NAV array should be: Overview (LayoutDashboard), Search (Search icon), Triage (ListChecks), Action Items (CircleCheckBig), Ingestion (Workflow), Knowledge (BookOpen), Settings (Settings). Total: 7 items. Sources and Messenger are removed from the rail but remain accessible via Settings sub-tabs at /settings/sources and /settings/messenger.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype's NAV array in shell.jsx lines 10-18 shows exactly this structure: 7 items with Search added at position 2, and Sources/Messenger removed from the main nav. The context summary confirms 'Sources and Messenger pages are used both as standalone routes (/sources, /messenger) and embedded within Settings sub-tabs (via the embedded prop).' This matches the dual-use pattern described.

decisions.question: What new route needs to be added for the Search page?
decisions.answer: Add route '/search' pointing to a new SearchPage component. The page implements master/detail layout: left panel with search input, kind filter (All/Diffs/Email/Meetings/Chat), and result list (340px sticky); right panel with rich item detail view including LLM summary, contextual payload (diff/email/meeting/chat renderers), full funnel processing log, and item actions.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype includes a complete SearchPage implementation in page-search.jsx with all the specified features. The existing App.tsx routing needs to add this route between / and /triage to match the nav order. The page structure is well-defined in the design summary.

decisions.question: How should Settings sub-tabs for Sources and Messenger be implemented?
decisions.answer: Modify Settings.tsx to add a tab bar with three tabs: System (existing content), Sources (renders Sources page with embedded=true prop), Messenger (renders Messenger page with embedded=true prop). Add routes /settings/sources and /settings/messenger. The Sources and Messenger components need an optional 'embedded' prop to conditionally hide page headers when rendered within Settings.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype's shell.jsx contextLabel function (lines 24-25) explicitly maps /settings/sources → SOURCES.CONFIG and /settings/messenger → MESSENGER. The design summary states: 'The embedded prop allows SourcesPage and MessengerPage to be used both standalone (at /sources, /messenger) and embedded within the settings tabs. This is a reuse pattern.' The existing Settings.tsx is currently a single page without tabs.

decisions.question: What TypeScript types/interfaces are needed for the Search page?
decisions.answer: SearchItem type with: id, kind ('diff'|'email'|'meeting'|'chat'), state (using existing ItemStatus enum), priority (existing Priority enum), relevance (number), summary, source, created_at, tags (string[]), llm_summary (string), context (union type: DiffContext | EmailContext | MeetingContext | ChatContext), log (Stage[] - reuse from funnel types), verdict (existing verdict structure). Context types need: DiffContext (author, team, status, url, hunks), EmailContext (from, to, when, body), MeetingContext (when, duration, location, attendees, agenda), ChatContext (channel, messages[]).
decisions.rationale: The design prototype's page-search.jsx and the data.js mock show searchItems[] with all these fields. The existing codebase has ItemStatus and Priority enums in api-types.ts. The context types are clearly defined in the contextual payload renderers (lines 42-114 of page-search.jsx). These types align with the existing domain vocabulary.

decisions.question: What new API endpoint is needed for the Search page?
decisions.answer: GET /api/search already exists and is used by the command palette (useSearch hook). The Search page can reuse this endpoint but may need different query parameters: add optional 'kind' filter (diff/email/meeting/chat) and increase limit (palette uses 20, page might need 50+). The endpoint returns SearchResponse with groups (items, actions, sources, facts) - the Search page will only use the 'items' group and client-side filter by kind.
decisions.rationale: The existing useSearch hook (hooks/useSearch.ts) already calls GET /api/search with q and limit parameters. The command palette uses it successfully. However, the Search page needs richer item data (full context, log, verdict) than the palette's SearchHit type provides. Either the endpoint needs to return fuller item data when limit is higher, or the page needs to fetch individual items after search. The design prototype doesn't show server interactions, only window.WB.searchItems.

decisions.question: What new TanStack Query hooks are needed?
decisions.answer: Create useSearchItems(query, kind, limit) hook that wraps the existing GET /api/search but returns full SearchItem[] instead of SearchHit[]. The hook should enable only when query.length >= 2 (matching SEARCH_MIN_CHARS), use placeholderData to keep prior results visible while fetching, and staleTime of 30s. May also need useItemActions(itemId) hook for the action buttons (set priority, mark done, snooze, archive, delete) unless these can reuse existing action hooks.
decisions.rationale: The pattern matches the existing useSearch hook structure. However, whether to create a new hook or extend useSearch depends on the API response shape. The Search page also needs item action mutations - the existing useActions hooks are for action items, not generic items. We may need new mutations for item-level operations or extend existing ones.

decisions.question: What existing components need modification for the Settings tabs?
decisions.answer: Modify Settings.tsx to add tab bar UI (role=tablist, tab buttons with aria-selected, content conditional on active tab). Modify Sources.tsx and Messenger.tsx to accept optional 'embedded' prop and conditionally hide page title when embedded=true. The tab active state should derive from pathname (/settings → system, /settings/sources → sources, /settings/messenger → messenger). No new shadcn components needed - use native button elements with custom styling matching the design prototype's tab pattern.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype's SettingsPage (in shell design context) shows the tab bar implementation pattern with inline buttons and conditional rendering. The embedded pattern is explicitly documented. The existing Settings.tsx needs restructuring but Sources and Messenger pages only need minor conditional rendering changes.

decisions.question: What about the breadcrumb navigation shown in the design?
decisions.answer: Add a Breadcrumb component that renders when route !== '/'. It shows '< Back to {label}' button in mono uppercase (11px, .04em tracking). For /triage/* routes, back goes to /triage. For all other routes, back goes to /. The component should render inside AppShell's main area, above page content (in the wb-main-inner div before children), with 12px bottom margin.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype's shell.jsx lines 240-251 show the exact Breadcrumb implementation. The context summary explicitly states: 'Breadcrumb: Renders only when route is not /. Shows a < Back to {label} button in mono uppercase.' The existing AppShell.tsx does not have this feature. It should be added as a component that consumes useLocation to determine back target.

decisions.question: Does the TopBar need changes for the breadcrumb pattern?
decisions.answer: No changes needed to TopBar. The breadcrumb is separate and renders inside the main content area, not in the TopBar. The TopBar keeps its current structure: brand mark, context label, command palette trigger, sync status, theme toggle, user chip. The contextLabel function needs to add a mapping for /search → 'SEARCH'.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype keeps TopBar unchanged (shell.jsx lines 70-99) and adds breadcrumb as a separate component (lines 240-251). The breadcrumb lives in the main content flow, not the sticky header. The only TopBar change needed is adding the /search context label mapping which is trivial.

decisions.question: What testing strategy is needed for the new Search page?
decisions.answer: Create SearchPage.test.tsx with: (1) renders empty state when no item selected, (2) search input auto-focuses on mount, (3) client-side kind filtering works, (4) clicking result row selects item and shows detail, (5) item actions trigger correct mutations with toast notifications, (6) contextual renderers (Diff/Email/Meeting/Chat) display correctly, (7) funnel log renders with FunnelStage components, (8) verdict pill shows current state. Mock the useSearchItems hook and action mutation hooks. Test keyboard interaction (Enter to search, arrow keys for result navigation) is optional but recommended.
decisions.rationale: The existing page tests (pages/*.test.tsx) follow this pattern: render states, user interactions, data display, action handlers. The Search page has complex master/detail interaction, multiple context renderers, and action buttons - all testable with @testing-library/react. The design prototype shows client-side filtering (no server call per kind change) so tests should verify that behavior.

decisions.question: Are there accessibility considerations for the hover-expand rail?
decisions.answer: Yes. Labels must remain accessible even when visually hidden (opacity: 0). Use aria-label on each NavLink button. Ensure focus-visible outline is visible during hover-expanded state. The rail expansion on hover should respect prefers-reduced-motion (disable transition). Keyboard users navigating via Tab should trigger the expanded state, not just mouse hover - consider :focus-within on wb-rail-nav to expand when any child has focus.
decisions.rationale: The existing AppSidebar already uses aria-label on NavLinks (line 70). The design prototype's CSS (app.css line 54) has focus-visible styling. However, the hover-expand is currently mouse-only - keyboard focus should also expand the rail for equity. The labels at opacity 0 with pointer-events: none (app.css line 50) are still in the DOM for screen readers, which is correct.

decisions.question: Are there performance concerns with the Search page?
decisions.answer: Potential concerns: (1) rendering large result lists - virtualize if 100+ results, (2) client-side text search across all fields could be slow with 1000+ items - debounce input and consider server-side search, (3) the funnel log trace in detail view can be expensive if stages[] is long - limit visible stages or paginate. The design shows max 60 items in memory which is fine for client-side filtering. Use React.memo for ResultRow to prevent re-renders when selection changes.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype uses client-side filtering (filter items by q.toLowerCase().includes) which works for small datasets but won't scale to 10k+ items. The existing useSearch hook already debounces at 200ms and does server-side search. The Search page should follow the same pattern. The funnel trace rendering performance depends on log complexity - the design's FunnelStage component should be memoized.

decisions.question: What CSS changes are needed for the hover-expand rail beyond the component?
decisions.answer: Add custom CSS to index.css or a new shell.css module: .wb-rail-nav class with position: absolute, width transition (64px → 216px on hover, 0.18s ease), box-shadow on hover (var(--shadow-pop)), overflow: hidden. .wb-rail-label with opacity transition (0 → 1 on parent hover, 0.14s ease). .wb-rail-item.is-active::before for the 2px orange left bar. @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to disable transitions. The existing Tailwind setup can handle most of this via custom classes but the hover parent-child relationship may need CSS.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype's app.css lines 25-59 show the exact CSS needed. Tailwind v4 can handle most of this (group-hover, transition utilities) but the complex hover state (expand nav, fade in all labels, add shadow) is cleaner as custom CSS. The existing index.css has theme tokens and primitives - shell-specific layout CSS should be co-located or imported as a module.

decisions.question: How should the SearchPage component be structured for maintainability?
decisions.answer: Extract sub-components into separate files: components/search/ResultRow.tsx, components/search/SearchItemDetail.tsx, components/search/contextual/ folder with DiffContext.tsx, EmailContext.tsx, MeetingContext.tsx, ChatContext.tsx. Keep filtering logic and state in the main SearchPage component. The contextual renderers are reusable (could be used in other item detail views) so they should be in components/search/ not inline. Use a barrel export (components/search/index.ts) to keep imports clean.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype puts everything in one file (page-search.jsx is 400+ lines per the 150-line sample). The existing codebase prefers modular components (DiffHunks is separate, FactRow is separate). The contextual renderers are domain-specific and could grow - email might add attachments, diffs might add code review UI. Splitting now prevents the page from becoming unmaintainable.

decisions.question: Should the command palette search also show full item context or keep current minimal SearchHit?
decisions.answer: Keep the command palette's SearchHit minimal (label, sublabel, route). The palette is for quick navigation, not inspection. The Search page is for deep exploration. The two use cases are distinct and should have different data shapes. Do not overload the SearchHit type with context/log/verdict - those are Search page concerns only.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype shows the palette returns only label/sub/route (shell.jsx lines 106-124) while the search page uses full items with context (data.js searchItems). The palette is a quick-jump tool (Cmd+K, type, hit Enter) - showing full diff hunks there would be overwhelming. The existing useSearch hook serves the palette well; create a separate hook for the Search page.

decisions.question: What happens to existing /sources and /messenger routes?
decisions.answer: Keep the standalone routes (/sources, /messenger) for backward compatibility and direct access. Also add /settings/sources and /settings/messenger. The AppSidebar nav removes these routes but they remain accessible via: (1) Settings tabs, (2) direct URL navigation, (3) command palette search, (4) internal links (e.g., SourceForm 'connection picker' navigation). Update the Sources and Messenger page components to accept an 'embedded' prop that hides the page header when true.
decisions.rationale: The design summary explicitly states: 'Sources and Messenger pages are used both as standalone routes (/sources, /messenger) and embedded within Settings sub-tabs (via the embedded prop). This is a reuse pattern -- the same page components serve two contexts.' Removing the routes would break direct links and internal navigation. The rail removal is a UX simplification, not a route deletion.

decisions.question: What new React pages are needed?
decisions.answer: Two new pages: (1) FiltersPage (IngestionFunnel) - unified interleaved funnel view with filters, enrichers, loopbacks, and funnel output table; (2) SearchPage - master/detail corpus search with full item context and funnel traces. Both are fully defined in the design prototype but do not exist in the current codebase.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype has complete implementations at page-filters.jsx (723 lines) and page-search.jsx (290 lines). The existing codebase has no /filters or /search routes in App.tsx. The Ingestion page exists but is focused on job monitoring, not the funnel. These are net-new pages with distinct purposes.

decisions.question: What new API endpoints are needed for the filters/enrichers/funnel flow?
decisions.answer: Six new GET endpoints: /api/filter-rules (already exists but needs enrichment), /api/enrichers (new - list all enrichers with config/stats), /api/loopbacks (new - list loop-back stages), /api/funnel-items (new - recent items with full stage traces), /api/enrichment-samples (new - sample context per enricher), /api/flow-matrix (new - source->output flow volumes for SourceFlow chart). Plus PATCH /api/filter-rules/{id} (enable/disable/reorder), DELETE /api/filter-rules/{id}, PATCH /api/enrichers/{id} (toggle), PATCH /api/loopbacks/{id} (toggle). The /api/filter-rules POST endpoint exists but needs validation for the new schema (prompt, action, sources array, confidence, origin).
decisions.rationale: The design data.js defines filterRules (9 entries), enrichers (4 entries), loopbacks (1 entry), funnelItems (9 items with stages arrays), enrichmentSamples (keyed by enricher ID). The existing filter_rules.py only has GET /filter-rules, POST /filter-rules, GET /filter-rules/{source_type}. The design's FilterRuleCard uses onToggle/onDelete/onMove callbacks, FilterDetailDialog reads processed items by filterId, EnricherDetailDialog reads samples by enricher.id. None of these data sources exist server-side yet.

decisions.question: What API endpoints are needed for the search page?
decisions.answer: One enhanced endpoint: GET /api/search needs to return full Item objects with context payloads (diff hunks, email body, meeting, chat messages), llm_summary, tags, funnel log (stages array), and verdict. The existing /api/search (used by CommandPalette) only returns lightweight search results (id, summary, type). We need either a new /api/items/search with full hydration or a query param on /api/items (?q=...) that filters the corpus and includes all enrichment/funnel data. Also need item action endpoints: PATCH /api/items/{id} (priority, state), POST /api/items/{id}/snooze, DELETE /api/items/{id}. Some of these exist (PATCH /api/items/{item_id}) but may need schema updates for the new fields (tags, llm_summary, context, log, verdict).
decisions.rationale: The design searchItems array (8 entries in data.js) includes kind, state, priority, relevance, tags[], llm_summary (personalized), context (type-specific payloads with hunks/body/messages), log (funnel stages), and verdict (decision/priority/confidence/rationale). The existing Item domain model (items.py) has id, summary, priority, status, created_at, updated_at, but no tags/llm_summary/context/log/verdict fields. The SearchItemDetail component renders DiffContext, EmailContext, MeetingContext, ChatContext - all require structured context payloads not currently in the Item schema.

decisions.question: What API endpoints are needed for the feedback correction loop?
decisions.answer: Four new endpoints: POST /api/feedback/corrections (record a filter classification override), DELETE /api/feedback/corrections/{item_id}/{filter_id} (undo), GET /api/feedback/tasks (list filter-tuning tasks), POST /api/feedback/tasks/{task_id}/apply (auto-apply refined prompt), POST /api/feedback/tasks/{task_id}/dismiss. The feedback store (feedback.js) is client-side only in the design - we need server persistence. Alternatively, tuning tasks could be action items with a special category='filter-tuning'.
decisions.rationale: The design's feedback.js implements WBFeedback as a pure client-side store with overrides[], tasks[], promptPatches{}. The FunnelStage component calls fb.addOverride() and fb.removeOverride(), FilterTuningCard (on Actions page) calls fb.autoApply(taskId) and fb.dismissTask(taskId). For production, this state must persist server-side - corrections inform future LLM calls, tuning tasks need to survive page reload. The design doesn't specify persistence, so we must decide: dedicated feedback tables or reuse action_items with metadata.

decisions.question: What new domain models or schema changes are required?
decisions.answer: Seven new or extended models: (1) FilterRule - add fields: prompt (str), action (enum: drop/include/label/context), sources (list), confidence (int 0-100), origin (enum: learned/explicit), matched (int), enabled (bool), label (optional str for action=label); (2) Enricher (new) - id, type, label, enabled, depth (shallow/deep), adds (list of field names), records (list of entity types), budget (max_calls, max_time_ms), enriched (int count), avg_calls, avg_ms; (3) LoopBack (new) - id, label, enabled, kind='loopback', trigger, condition, max_loops, looped (count), avg_loops; (4) FunnelStage (new, embedded) - filterId, outcome (enum), confidence, reason, context, label, weak (bool); (5) Item - add fields: tags (list), llm_summary (str), context (JSON), log/stages (list of FunnelStage), verdict (decision/priority/confidence/rationale); (6) Verdict (new, embedded) - decision (queued/dropped/triaged), priority, confidence, rationale; (7) FeedbackCorrection (new) - id, item_id, filter_id, from_outcome, to_outcome, to_label, created_at.
decisions.rationale: The design data structures are explicit in data.js. The existing FilterRule (filters.py) only has id, source_type, pattern, action, priority, created_from_interaction_id - missing prompt, sources array, confidence, origin, matched, enabled, label. The Item model (items.py) has 8 fields; the design searchItems need 15+ fields. Enrichers, LoopBacks, FunnelStage, Verdict, FeedbackCorrection do not exist in the domain/ package at all.

decisions.question: What new shared React components are needed?
decisions.answer: Fourteen new components: (1) ActionChip - color-coded outcome badge (drop/include/label/context/pass/skip/loopback); (2) ConfidenceBar - horizontal progress bar with percentage; (3) VerdictPill - final verdict indicator with decision/priority/confidence; (4) SourceChip - inline source icon+name chip; (5) StateDot - colored dot+label for item state; (6) FunnelStage - single stage in item funnel trace with correction UI; (7) ItemFunnelDialog - full per-item provenance modal; (8) FilterRuleCard - ordered filter card with reorder/toggle/delete; (9) FilterDetailDialog - filter's processed items with correction summary; (10) EnricherCard - enricher card with stats/budget/samples; (11) EnricherDetailDialog - enricher samples detail view; (12) LoopBackCard - loop-back stage card; (13) DiffHunks - collapsible diff viewer (may already exist in components/); (14) Portal - ReactDOM.createPortal wrapper for dialogs. Plus context renderers: DiffContext, EmailContext, MeetingContext, ChatContext for SearchPage.
decisions.rationale: The design primitives.jsx exports Icon, Skeleton, EmptyState, Dialog, Menu, SectionHeader, StateLoading, StateError, StateUnauthorized, Portal, useFeedbackStore. The existing codebase components/ has EmptyState, Skeleton, but not Dialog/Menu/Portal/SectionHeader. The design page-filters.jsx defines 9 sub-components inline (SourceChip, ActionChip, ConfidenceBar, VerdictPill, FilterRuleCard, FilterDetailDialog, FunnelStage, ItemFunnelDialog, EnricherCard, EnricherDetailDialog, LoopBackCard, AddRuleDialog). The design page-search.jsx defines 6 sub-components (StateDot, ResultRow, DiffContext, EmailContext, MeetingContext, ChatContext, ItemContext, SearchItemDetail). DiffHunks is referenced in both pages. The existing codebase has DiffHunks.tsx in components/ (117 lines), so we can reuse that.

decisions.question: What new TanStack Query hooks are needed?
decisions.answer: Twelve new hooks: (1) useFilterRules() - GET /api/filter-rules with polling; (2) useEnrichers() - GET /api/enrichers; (3) useLoopbacks() - GET /api/loopbacks; (4) useFunnelItems() - GET /api/funnel-items; (5) useEnrichmentSamples(enricherId) - GET /api/enrichment-samples/{id}; (6) useFlowMatrix() - GET /api/flow-matrix for SourceFlow chart; (7) useToggleFilterRule() - PATCH /api/filter-rules/{id} mutation; (8) useDeleteFilterRule() - DELETE /api/filter-rules/{id}; (9) useReorderFilterRules() - PATCH /api/filter-rules/order (new endpoint); (10) useItemSearch(query, kind) - GET /api/items/search?q=...&kind=...; (11) useItemActions() - mutations for PATCH /api/items/{id}, DELETE /api/items/{id}, POST /api/items/{id}/snooze; (12) useFeedbackCorrections() - GET /api/feedback/corrections, POST mutations. Plus a custom useFeedbackStore() hook wrapping WBFeedback client store for React subscriptions.
decisions.rationale: The design pages reference data from window.WB (mock data). For production, each data source needs a hook. The FiltersPage reads filterRules, enrichers, loopbacks, funnelItems, enrichmentSamples - none of these have existing hooks. The SearchPage reads searchItems - the existing useSearch hook (for command palette) is different. The design feedback.js exports useFeedbackStore() as a React subscription wrapper. The existing hooks/ directory has useStats, useItems, useTriage, useActions, useSources, useFacts, useMessenger, useSettings, useTopology, useSearch, useWorkMode - none cover filters/enrichers/funnel/feedback.

decisions.question: What new storage repositories are needed?
decisions.answer: Five new repository interfaces + PostgreSQL implementations: (1) FilterRulesStore - get_rules(), add_rule(), update_rule(id, enabled/prompt), delete_rule(id), reorder_rules(order); (2) EnrichersStore - get_enrichers(), update_enricher(id, enabled); (3) LoopBacksStore - get_loopbacks(), update_loopback(id, enabled); (4) FunnelTracesStore - get_recent_items_with_traces(limit), get_item_trace(item_id); (5) FeedbackStore - add_correction(), get_corrections_for_filter(filter_id), delete_correction(item_id, filter_id), add_tuning_task(), get_open_tasks(), apply_task(task_id), dismiss_task(task_id). The existing stores (storage/postgres/) have ItemStore, TriageStore, IngestionQueueStore, SourceStore, JobStore - none of these cover the new entities.
decisions.rationale: The design data structures (filterRules, enrichers, loopbacks, funnelItems, enrichmentSamples, feedback state) have no storage layer in the existing codebase. The existing filter_rules.py API references stores.filter_rules, which does not exist in storage/. The repository pattern (storage/README.md) requires one interface per domain entity. Enrichers are provider config, not stored data - but their stats (enriched count, avg_ms) need persistence. FunnelTraces are item metadata - could be JSON columns on items table or a separate funnel_stages table. Feedback corrections are user input that must persist across sessions.

decisions.question: What database migrations are required?
decisions.answer: Four new tables + schema changes: (1) filter_rules table - id, prompt, action, sources (JSON array), confidence, origin, matched, enabled, label, created_at, updated_at, order_index; (2) enricher_stats table - enricher_id (references provider config), enriched_count, avg_calls, avg_ms, last_run; (3) loopback_stats table - loopback_id, looped_count, avg_loops; (4) feedback_corrections table - id, item_id, filter_id, from_outcome, from_label, to_outcome, to_label, created_at; (5) ALTER items table - add columns: tags (JSON array), llm_summary (text), context (JSONB), funnel_log (JSONB array of stages), verdict_decision (enum), verdict_priority (enum), verdict_confidence (int), verdict_rationale (text). Alternative: store funnel_log/verdict in a separate item_verdicts table if items get too wide.
decisions.rationale: The existing migrations/ has schema for items, triage_cards, ingestion_queue, sources, jobs, memory tables. None of the new entities (FilterRule, Enricher stats, LoopBack stats, FeedbackCorrection, Item.tags/llm_summary/context/log/verdict) exist in the schema. The design's domain models require persistent storage for all fields shown in data.js. The Item extension (tags, llm_summary, context, log, verdict) adds 8 new columns - manageable as ALTER but consider normalization for funnel_log if stage count grows large.

decisions.question: What chart/visualization components need to be added or modified?
decisions.answer: Two new chart components: (1) MultiLineChart - multi-series smooth line chart with hover tooltip, legend, HTML axis overlay (used for throughput chart on Actions page); (2) SourceFlow - animated Sankey flow visualization showing items flowing from sources through WorkBench to outputs (Action Items, Triage Queue, Filtered Out, Errors) with animated dots, hover interactions, stalled-source detection (used on Overview or new Dashboard page). The existing charts.jsx (from design prototype) has both implementations. The existing codebase ui/src/components/ has ChartCard, but uses Recharts (AreaChart, BarChart, PieChart) - SourceFlow and MultiLineChart are custom SVG.
decisions.rationale: The design charts.jsx exports MultiLineChart (new, 132px default height, Catmull-Rom curves, per-series data[], hover tooltip with edge-flip) and SourceFlow (new, animated Bezier ribbons, flow matrix M[source][output], dot animation via RAF). The existing Overview.tsx uses Recharts. The design's ActionItems page references a throughput chart (MultiLineChart with incoming vs completion series). The design mentions SourceFlow on the Overview but the existing Overview.tsx doesn't have it - this is a new addition.

decisions.question: What new TypeScript types/interfaces are needed beyond domain models?
decisions.answer: Fifteen new types: (1) FilterRule (client) - matches server but adds tuned:boolean for UI; (2) Enricher - id, type, label, enabled, depth, adds[], records[], budget, enriched, avg_calls, avg_ms; (3) LoopBack - id, label, enabled, kind, trigger, condition, max_loops, looped, avg_loops; (4) FunnelStage - filterId, outcome, confidence, reason, context, label, weak; (5) Verdict - decision, priority, confidence, rationale; (6) FunnelItem - id, summary, source, created_at, verdict, stages[]; (7) SearchItem - extends Item with tags[], llm_summary, context (union type), log[], verdict; (8) DiffContext - type='diff', author, team, status, url, hunks[]; (9) EmailContext - type='email', from, to, when, body; (10) MeetingContext - type='meeting', when, duration, location, attendees[], agenda; (11) ChatContext - type='chat', channel, messages[]; (12) ItemContext - union of Diff/Email/Meeting/ChatContext; (13) FeedbackCorrection - itemId, filterId, fromOutcome, toOutcome, etc; (14) FilterTuningTask - id, kind, status, proposedPrompt, ...; (15) FlowMatrix - M: Record<Source, Record<Output, number>>.
decisions.rationale: The design data.js defines explicit shapes for all entities. The existing api-types.ts (auto-generated from OpenAPI) will not have these until the server schema is updated. The UI components need client-side types immediately for development. The context union type (DiffContext | EmailContext | MeetingContext | ChatContext) is used by ItemContext component and SearchItemDetail. The FeedbackCorrection and FilterTuningTask types match the feedback.js store schema.

decisions.question: What accessibility considerations are critical for the new features?
decisions.answer: Eight a11y requirements: (1) Keyboard navigation in FiltersPage - reorder buttons must be keyboard-accessible (arrow keys + Enter, or up/down buttons with proper focus management); (2) FilterDetailDialog, ItemFunnelDialog, EnricherDetailDialog - modal dialogs need focus trap, Escape to close, aria-modal, aria-labelledby; (3) SearchPage master/detail - result list must be keyboard-navigable (j/k keys or arrow keys), selected item indicated by aria-current or similar; (4) FunnelStage correction picker - 'correct' button + inline form must be keyboard-operable, focus returns to button on cancel; (5) ActionChip, VerdictPill, StateDot - ensure color + text/icon redundancy (not color-only); (6) SourceFlow animated chart - provide static text fallback or ARIA live region announcing flow changes; (7) MultiLineChart hover tooltip - ensure keyboard users can access data (keyboard-navigable data table alternative or aria-describedby); (8) Toast notifications - use role='status' (already in design), auto-dismiss with adequate duration (design: 2.2s).
decisions.rationale: The design prototype uses semantic HTML (button, form, table, dialog) and includes some ARIA (aria-label, aria-modal, role='dialog', role='status'). The existing codebase ADR 0046 enforces contrast requirements. The new features add complex interactions: reorderable lists (drag-and-drop alternative needed), modal dialogs (focus management critical), master/detail (keyboard nav), inline editing (correction picker). The design's SearchPage already supports j/k keyboard nav. The SourceFlow chart is purely visual - needs a11y fallback.

decisions.question: What are the primary performance concerns?
decisions.answer: Six performance considerations: (1) FunnelItems query - fetching all recent items with full stage arrays could be expensive; implement pagination or limit to last 100 items, index on created_at; (2) EnrichmentSamples - per-enricher sample data is large (context key/value pairs); lazy-load on dialog open, not on page mount; (3) SearchPage corpus - full-text search across all items with context payloads is heavy; implement server-side search with limit (max 100 results), debounce client input (design: none specified, recommend 300ms); (4) ItemFunnelDialog - rendering 10+ FunnelStage components with timing calculations; memoize stageTimings(), use React.memo for FunnelStage; (5) SourceFlow animation - requestAnimationFrame loop for dot movement; pause animation when tab hidden (visibilitychange event); (6) FilterRules/Enrichers reordering - optimistic updates to avoid UI lag, rollback on server error.
decisions.rationale: The design data.js has 9 funnelItems, 4 enrichers, 8 searchItems - realistic for a demo but production could have 1000s. The ItemFunnelDialog calls itemLog(item), stageTimings(log) on every render - needs memoization. The SourceFlow uses setInterval + RAF for dot animation - needs cleanup on unmount and pause on hidden. The existing codebase uses TanStack Query with 15s-60s polling - the new endpoints should follow this pattern but avoid polling for large datasets (funnel items, search results). The design's SearchPage has no pagination - needs to be added.

decisions.question: What testing strategy should be used for the new features?
decisions.answer: Five-layer testing approach: (1) Unit tests for helpers - ruleById(), itemLog(), stageTimings(), enricherStageFor(), refinedPrompt() (feedback.js); use deterministic fixtures; (2) Component tests - ActionChip, ConfidenceBar, VerdictPill, SourceChip, StateDot, FunnelStage (with and without correction), FilterRuleCard, EnricherCard, LoopBackCard; test visual states, interactions, keyboard nav; (3) Integration tests - FilterDetailDialog with mock items, ItemFunnelDialog with mock log, EnricherDetailDialog with mock samples; test dialog open/close, item click handlers; (4) Page tests - FiltersPage with mock data (rules, enrichers, loopbacks, items), SearchPage with mock corpus; test filtering, reordering, correction flow, item actions; (5) API tests - new endpoints with test database, verify schema, pagination, error handling. Use MSW for mocking in component/page tests. Existing pattern: *.test.tsx files next to components/pages, using @testing-library/react + Vitest.
decisions.rationale: The existing codebase has comprehensive test coverage - every page has a .test.tsx file (14 test files total), components/ has test files for primitives, hooks/ has useTriageCard.test.ts and useWorkMode.test.ts. The design introduces ~20 new components and 4 helper functions - all need tests. The feedback correction loop is complex (multi-step user flow) - needs integration tests. The new API endpoints need server-side tests (pytest) to verify data integrity, especially reordering logic and feedback persistence.

decisions.question: What new React component is needed for the Live Funnel Tail?
decisions.answer: Create a new `LiveTail.tsx` component that renders a structured table with 5 columns (Time, Item ID, Source, Funnel stage, Status). The component will: (1) flatten funnelItems into item+stage event pool, (2) stream new rows at 2.1s intervals via setInterval, (3) maintain max 60 rows, (4) auto-scroll to bottom on new rows, (5) apply 'wb-tail-new' CSS class to newest row for flash animation, (6) make rows clickable to open ItemFunnelDialog, (7) accept onOpenItem callback and paused prop, (8) use ActionChip for status column, (9) show enricher stages in tertiary color and filter stages in brand color.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype shows a complete LiveTail component with clear requirements. It's a structured table replacing the unstructured LogStream. All visual and interaction patterns are specified. The component maps directly to existing patterns (DataTable structure, auto-scroll from LogStream, ActionChip from filters page).

Use STAGE_META constant for colors and icons. Render as inline-flex chip with icon, action label, optional confidence percentage. Handle special case for 'label' action to show 'label: {label}' format.

The design prototype provides exact styling, color mappings, and behavior. This will be reusable across LiveTail, filter cards, and funnel traces.

Color values: drop uses red tones (#ffb4ab fg, color-mix red bg), include uses success green, label uses purple (#b79cf7), context uses tertiary cyan, pass/skip use muted colors.

Extracting to a constants file follows the pattern of CHART_COLORS in lib/chart-theme.ts and enables consistency across all funnel visualizations.

Should return last 50-100 items, ordered by created_at desc. The endpoint should be polled at 15-30s interval like other stats endpoints.

If extending /api/items, could be useItems({include_stages: true}). The hook should handle loading/error states per the five-state taxonomy and provide the data for LiveTail component to flatten into events.
decisions.rationale: All data-fetching in the current codebase uses TanStack Query with the pollWhenVisible helper (see useActivity, useJobs, etc). The pattern is established and consistent. The only uncertainty is the exact endpoint path and parameter shape, but the hook structure is certain. The 30s poll matches other stats endpoints while keeping data fresh enough for a 'live' experience.

decisions.question: What CSS is needed for the live tail flash animation?
decisions.answer: Add to index.css: (1) .wb-tail-new class with animation: wb-tail-flash 1.1s ease; (2) @keyframes wb-tail-flash with 0% background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 12%, transparent), 100% background: transparent. Also add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) override to disable animation. This creates a subtle flash when new rows appear, matching the design pattern used in LogStream's polite updates.

decisions.question: What UI control is needed for live/paused toggle and how should it work?
decisions.answer: Add a toggle button in the SectionHeader right slot: inline-flex with dot indicator (7px circle, animated pulse when live, static when paused), 'live'/'paused' label, and Play/Pause icon. Use aria-pressed for accessibility. Button style: rounded border, green-tinted background when live (color-mix success 12%), transparent when paused. State stored in tailLive boolean, toggled by setTailLive. When paused=true, LiveTail's useEffect returns early without starting setInterval.

decisions.question: How should the component flatten funnelItems into a streamable event pool?
decisions.answer: In LiveTail: (1) useMemo to iterate funnelItems, for each item iterate its stages, push {item, stage} objects to pool array; (2) use a cursor ref (initialized to random pool index) to track position; (3) on mount, generate initial 9 rows with sequential cursor increments and decreasing timestamps (now - index*4200ms); (4) on interval, append mkRow(cursor++, Date.now()), slice to last 60; (5) mkRow generates unique key from cursor+item.id and creates {key, t, item, stage} row object; (6) increment cursor.current modulo pool.length to cycle.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype provides exact implementation in LiveTail function: useMemo for pool, useRef for cursor, useState with initializer for rows, mkRow helper, setInterval logic, slice(-60) cap. This is a complete algorithm with no ambiguity. The only adaptation needed is replacing window.WB.funnelItems with the TanStack Query hook result.

Create ActionChip.test.tsx: render each action type, verify icon/label/colors. Mock useFunnelItems hook in MSW test server. Use vi.useFakeTimers for interval tests.

decisions.question: What accessibility features are needed for the Live Funnel Tail?
decisions.answer: Add: (1) role='table' on container with role='columnheader' on headers and role='row'/'cell' on data rows (or use semantic table elements); (2) aria-label='Live funnel tail' on section; (3) aria-live='polite' on scrollable container so screen readers announce new rows without interrupting; (4) aria-pressed on live/paused toggle button; (5) keyboard focus ring on clickable rows with :focus-visible; (6) title attribute on each row button describing the action; (7) respect prefers-reduced-motion for auto-scroll and flash animation.
decisions.rationale: The design prototype uses button elements for rows (good for a11y), includes title attributes, and references aria-expanded. Current codebase shows strong a11y patterns: LogStream uses role='log' + aria-live, DataTable uses semantic table elements, focus-visible rings are global. The Live Tail is essentially a clickable, live-updating table, so standard table a11y patterns apply. Prefers-reduced-motion is already used in LogStream and index.css.

decisions.question: What performance optimizations are needed for streaming updates?
decisions.answer: Implement: (1) useMemo for funnelItems pool flattening to prevent re-computation on unrelated renders; (2) useRef for cursor to avoid triggering re-renders on increment; (3) 60-row cap via slice(-60) to bound memory and DOM nodes; (4) cleanup function in useEffect to clearInterval on unmount/pause; (5) requestAnimationFrame for scroll updates instead of immediate scrollTop assignment; (6) React.memo on ActionChip if re-render profiling shows issues; (7) consider virtualizing rows if 60 rows causes scroll lag (unlikely but monitor).
decisions.rationale: The design prototype uses useMemo, useRef, and cleanup patterns correctly. These are React best practices. The 60-row cap is explicit. However, medium confidence because: (1) we haven't profiled the actual performance, (2) virtualization may be over-engineering for 60 rows, (3) the optimal polling interval (client animation vs server poll) affects data freshness vs load. The fundamentals are sound, but real-world performance depends on data volume and user behavior.

decisions.question: How should the feedback store be integrated?
decisions.answer: Create /home/anshulverma/workspace/workbench/ui/src/lib/feedback-store.ts as a TypeScript adaptation of the prototype's feedback.js. Export a singleton store with subscribe/addOverride/removeOverride/autoApply/dismissTask methods, plus a React hook useFeedbackStore() that subscribes and forces re-render. The store manages overrides[], tasks[], and promptPatches{} in module-level state.
decisions.rationale: The prototype uses a plain JS feedback store (feedback.js) loaded before React. The TypeScript codebase needs an equivalent. The store is a pub/sub singleton that tracks user corrections to filter classifications, generates tuning tasks with refinedPrompt(), and allows auto-applying prompt patches. The useFeedbackStore() hook (used in ActionsPage line 99) is a simple subscribe wrapper that returns the API object and forces re-render on state changes.

decisions.question: What new API endpoints are needed (server-side)?

Future enhancement: (1) GET /api/stats/throughput-timeseries?window=12h to replace mock data; (2) POST /api/filter-rules/{id}/prompt to persist auto-applied prompt patches.

The prototype is a design artifact, not a production implementation. For production: throughput needs a real endpoint, and prompt patches need persistence. But for v1 UI implementation, no server changes are required - just client-side state and mock data.

Following the existing test patterns in src/components/*.test.tsx and src/pages/*.test.tsx.

decisions.question: What accessibility considerations are needed?
decisions.answer: MultiLineChart: add aria-label with data summary, ensure tooltip is keyboard-accessible (add focus/blur handlers to trigger hover state), ensure color is not the only differentiator (legend labels). FilterTuningCard: ensure buttons have clear labels, task description is programmatically exposed. Filter tuning section: use semantic <section> with aria-label.
decisions.rationale: The existing codebase shows strong a11y practices (aria-labels on action rows, semantic HTML, focus management). The prototype's MultiLineChart has mouse-only hover interaction - keyboard users need an equivalent. Color-coding alone is insufficient per WCAG (legend text provides the secondary indicator). The FilterTuningCard buttons are adequately labeled in the prototype. The filter tuning section should follow the existing SectionHeader pattern with proper semantics.

decisions.question: Are there any performance concerns?
decisions.answer: Monitor: (1) MultiLineChart smoothPath() calculation on every mousemove - consider debouncing or memoizing the path string; (2) useFeedbackStore causing re-renders across all subscribed components - ensure listeners only subscribe to relevant state slices; (3) Rendering large task lists in filter tuning section - add virtualization if >20 tasks. For v1, these are acceptable; optimize if metrics show issues.
decisions.rationale: The prototype's MultiLineChart calculates smoothPath() and tooltip position on every mousemove (charts.jsx lines 293-298). For small datasets (12 points), this is fine. The feedback store emits to all listeners on any state change (feedback.js line 9) - if multiple components subscribe, they all re-render. The prototype is a single-page app with no optimization, suitable for design validation but may need refinement for production. React's built-in batching should handle the re-render storm from feedback store updates. No virtual scrolling in the prototype - fine for expected task counts (<10).

The existing implementation has the button in the header AND a FAB. The prototype shows the button in the header but ALSO has the FAB (not shown in the Actions page code but present in the shell).
